variant_reviews.comparison: Factor A=Q_A R_A with a compatible thin QR so R_A is square and invertible; normalized Gram-Schmidt can produce zero vectors for dependent columns and does not remove that requirement. Transform Y by Q_A-transpose on mode 1, obtain all initial mode subspaces, and refine using only U_j^0 factors. Project in transformed coordinates, then multiply mode 1 by R_A^-1. The nonsingular-inverse theorem requires unit determinant; Lean's singular inverse fallback is not a rank-deficient algorithm convention, and source unfolding/SVD tie choices remain separate.
